title: Managing freight carrier compliance paperwork on Mac: a guide for freight brokers
metaTitle: Managing freight carrier compliance paperwork: A guide for Mac users
description: Stop losing time on manual carrier vetting. Learn how to handle freight carrier compliance paperwork efficiently on your Mac without expensive software.
intro: Managing freight carrier compliance paperwork is a daily hurdle that often stops your dispatch flow. You need to verify insurance, FMCSA authority, and safety records before a load moves, but the constant tab switching on your Mac eats up your margin.
tldr: Carrier vetting is now a legal requirement to avoid negligent hiring lawsuits.

blocks.text: Why managing freight carrier compliance paperwork is difficult

The core of the problem is data fragmentation. You likely have your TMS open in one Chrome tab, your email in another, and a carrier vetting site like Carrier411 or Highway in a third. Moving between these windows to copy and paste MC numbers or verify insurance certificates is where errors happen. When you are under pressure to cover a load, these extra steps feel like a burden. This is when shortcuts get taken, and that is exactly what bad actors look for.
The real cost of poor compliance

The costs go beyond just lost time. A single fraudulent load can cost you your reputation and your bottom line. If a carrier double-brokers your load, you lose the cargo and face potential lawsuits. Recent court rulings have made it harder for brokers to defend against negligent hiring claims. You must show that you performed due diligence. If you cannot produce a timestamped record of why you chose one carrier over another, you are vulnerable.
Fixes you can use right now

items: Create a standard operating procedure for every load. Write down the hard-stop criteria like minimum time in business or specific insurance limits.
Use browser extensions that pull carrier data directly into your TMS or email. This keeps you in one window.
Set up automated alerts for insurance expiration. Do not rely on manual spreadsheet tracking.
Document every vetting decision. If a carrier is rejected, save the reason in your TMS. This protects you in court.
